messages.subject: DSSim package: difference between "make.detectability" and "make.ddf.analysis.list"
parts:
Hi Distance people, Maybe a silly question...

I can´t figure out the difference between what the commands "make.detectability" and "make.ddf.analysis.list" does.


make.detectability Creates a Detectablility object and make.ddf.analysis.list  creates a list of DDF.Analysis objects each of which describes a model to fit to the
distance data.


Both objects are used in "make.simulation" but, intuitively, "make.ddf.analysis.list" should prevail over "make.detectability". If so, what is the need of "make.detectability"?

Many thanks

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSSim package: difference between "make.detectability" and "make.ddf.analysis.list"
parts:
Adrian

Good question, but easy to put your mind at rest.

In constructing a simulation, specification needs to be made of the detection function the animals actually obey and a model the analyst fits to the observed data.  The two functions you mention perform these two jobs.  This recognises the reality that the analyst will not necessarily fit the true detection model.  The `make.ddf.analyst.list` can include more than one model, recognising an analyst will fit multiple models to a data set.

Hope that is clear.
